newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil reacts calmly to U.S. WTO move on cars.
newsitem.headline: Brazil reacts calmly to U.S. WTO move on cars.

text.p: Brazilian officials reacted calmly Friday to Washington's latest protest to the World Trade Organization over Brasilia's car industry rules, saying the U.S. move revealed "a spirit of dialogue".
Jose Alfredo Graca Lima, head of the Foreign Ministry's Economics Department, told reporters the call for formal consultations was "normal."
"This indicates there is a spirit of dialogue," Graca Lima said.

Earlier, a spokesman for the U.S. Trade Representative's Office said Washington had lodged a second request for formal talks over Brazil's car industry rules, which set lower import tariffs for automakers with Brazilian factories.
In August, it requested talks over the rules themselves.

On Friday, the USTR said it also wanted consultations over low tariff quotas for Japan, South Korea and the European Union and a new program which aims to attract car makers to Brazil's northeast, the north and the center-west. Argentina has also reacted with fury to the incentives, which involve zero tariffs for car part imports and tax breaks.
Graca Lima said the Brazilian government aimed to formally notify within the month the WTO's subsidies committee of the program for the regions and it would be discussed by the committee in April.
"We will present it as a subsidy for underprivileged areas," he said, adding that WTO rules for developing countries allowed for regional subsidies.

Brazil's Car Industry Rules have atrracted controversy since they were changed in December 1995 to allow manufacturers with a Brazilian base to import at a 35 percent tariff while outsiders face a stiff 70-percent duty.
It was intended to encourage investment and has persuaded a string of international car makers to announce they will build plants in Brazil.
